answer: An agent economy can make each identity earn a nontransferable reputation by completing work that a randomly chosen peer verifies against the result. A new identity starts with no standing; claims that affect payment or access require a bond, forfeited when an audit finds fraud. Splitting into many identities does not split the bond or create history, so a sybil attacker must lock up more capital and repeatedly produce verifiable work. A relic catalog, cedar shipment, or opal trade can all use the same rule.
